# Enter-to-end-turn browser wait exceeds the 60 s hook above ~2x CPU oversubscription

## Headline

The `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` wait in
`tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` is already at the largest
budget the 60 s browser hook permits (40 000 ms = 16 000 ms cap + 24 000 ms
margin + 20 000 ms boot = 60 000 ms), yet it fails at ≈2× CPU oversubscription
because the bounded end-of-turn deferral is re-polled on Phaser's clamped game
clock, so the forced day start is detected late. **Decision: make the
deferral's safety cap starvation-proof** — one extracted helper whose deadline
and re-poll run on wall clock, enforced even while the page is not painting
(producer, Q1 = C, Q2 = 1).

## Problem statement

The soak evidence on MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L shows the gate passes 20/20 quiet
(peak load 15.3), passes 2/2 at 8 burners (peak 23.6), and fails exactly one
wait — `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` — at load ≥ ≈31
(≈2× oversubscription, 16 burners, peak 32.8). That wait's budget is already at
the ceiling the 60 s hook permits, so no poll-budget tweak inside the hook can
rescue it.

Root cause (mechanism, verified against the installed `phaser` source):
Phaser's `TimeStep` clamps the per-frame delta it feeds scenes — under
`smoothStep` (default on) each frame contributes at most `1000/fps.min`
(200 ms) — and `Clock.elapsed`, which drives `delayedCall` timers and tween
progress, advances by that clamped delta. Under starvation (a few frames per
second) all game-time-paced choreography stretches: income phase gaps, coin
flights, the incident hold, and the deferral's own 250 ms `delayedCall`
re-polls. The deferral *deadline* (`s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`,
where `s.time.now` is the raw frame timestamp) is wall-clock, but it is only
re-checked at those clamped polls, so the forced day start is delayed by the
same starvation. Aggregate: closing choreography (stretched) + 16 s cap
(late-detected) + boot > the 40 s budget and the 60 s hook.

The cap's stated purpose is "end-of-turn can never hang the game"
(CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q, AC5/AC7). A stall bound that is only observed at frame
boundaries does not provide that guarantee — which is what this item fixes,
without touching the user-visible pacing.

## Users

- **Agent-implementer / gate runner** on the shared dev host: needs the browser
  gate green; a red `MainStreetScene` suite at ≈2× oversubscription burns whole
  sessions on retries and blocks the build → test → commit order.
- **Maintainer triaging a red browser suite**: needs a red wait to mean a
  behavioural regression, not host weather.
- **Release engineer** on the dev-push gate: a red gate on a loaded shared host
  stalls shipping even when the scene is correct.
- **Players**: unchanged pacing — the choreography, the incident hold and the
  cap value all stay as shipped; only the cap's *enforcement* becomes
  wall-clock rather than frame-clock, so under starvation the day advances at
  the documented bound instead of stalling past it.

Example user stories:

> As an agent running the browser gate on the shared 16-core host, I want the
> Enter-to-end-turn wait to pass at any load the host actually reaches, so that
> my gate result does not depend on which sibling suites happen to be running.

> As a player whose machine is momentarily overloaded, I want the end-of-turn
> to still advance within the documented safety window, so that the game can
> never appear hung.

## Existing state

- Measured envelope (2026-10-24, 16-core shared host): quiet 20/20 pass
  (peak 15.3); 8 burners 2/2 pass, then one fail at ambient 31.3; 16 burners
  fail at the 40 000 ms end-of-turn budget. Every other wait in the file passes
  at that load.
- The wait's effective budget is `capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` (16 000) +
  `floorMs: END_TURN_STARVATION_MARGIN_MS` (24 000) = 40 000 ms, the largest
  that keeps the documented 20 000 ms scene-boot allowance inside the 60 s
  `testTimeout` (asserted by `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`). The
  suite's per-test timeout is already `it(..., 60_000)`.
- Five deferral polls race the choreography, all with the same shape
  (`startAt = <scene clock> + cap`, then `delayedCall(250, poll)`):
  3 in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` (`advanceTurn` ~433,
  forced event-choice ~617, piggyback ~783) and 2 in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` (`finish`'s income wait
  ~254 and the reveal gating ~301).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` already has the
  degradation precedent: `scheduleOrRun` runs the callback immediately when the
  scene has no clock (headless), which a wall-clock helper must preserve.
- Node unit suites drive these polls through fake `time` stubs
  (`tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts`), and
  `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` pins "exactly three
  `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" by regex — both must be
  updated by the extraction.
- Reduced motion clears `incomeCollectionActive` synchronously in
  `MainStreetAnimatorIncome` (~line 1039), but it is **not** the remedy chosen:
  the parent rejected it as the sole remedy because it removes the
  deferred-income path from coverage.

## Desired change (decision: option C)

Replace the five duplicated deferral polls with **one shared, injectable
helper** that:

1. computes its deadline from a wall-clock timestamp (`Date.now()`),
2. re-polls with a wall-clock timer (`window.setTimeout`), not the scene clock,
3. forces completion (clearing `incomeCollectionActive` and invoking the
   caller's continuation) once `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` of wall time has
   elapsed since the deferral began,
4. is enforced even when the page is not painting — a backgrounded/hidden
   document ahead of the cap forces the advance rather than waiting for the
   next animation frame (Q2 = 1), and
5. degrades to today's behaviour where no clock/timer exists (headless node
   scenes run the continuation immediately), and exposes its clock/timer for
   deterministic unit driving.

Options considered and rejected (recorded for traceability):

- **A — accept and document the envelope** (no code change): the gate can still
  go red on the shared host when ambient load spikes ≥2×, conflicting with the
  "red tree never pushed" policy; rejected in favour of a root-cause fix.
- **B — reduced-motion Enter test + a separate cheap deferral-contract test**:
  no production change, but downgrades the file's end-to-end end-of-turn test
  to a synthetic and couples coverage to a reduced-motion implementation
  detail; retained only as a fallback if C's soak does not pass.
- **D — raise the browser hook for this test**: pure masking, requires
  amending the parent's "any derived budget must leave headroom for boot plus
  teardown within that hook" AC and re-baselining the guard's headroom rule,
  and would fail again at ≈4× oversubscription; rejected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **One bounded-deferral helper, wall-clock enforced.** All five
      income-collection deferral polls route through a single shared helper
      whose deadline is wall clock and whose re-poll is a wall timer; no inline
      `s.time.delayedCall(250, <poll>)` / `<scene clock> + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`
      poll remains. A unit test with a frozen scene clock and an advancing wall
      clock proves the continuation is forced within one poll interval of the
      16 000 ms cap.
- [ ] **Forced advance is not tied to paint.** When the document is hidden / no
      frame runs, the cap still forces the advance after the cap elapses
      (Q2 = 1). A unit test asserts the wall timer — not the scene clock —
      drives the assertion, and the behaviour is documented in the module's
      code comment.
- [ ] **Injectable and backward-compatible.** The helper accepts an injectable
      clock/timer (so `competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
      `turnflow.test.ts` and the new tests drive it deterministically) and
      preserves today's no-clock degradation (headless scenes run the
      continuation immediately).
- [ ] **Single source of truth for the cap.** `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` stays
      16 000 and remains the only cap value; the
      `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` "exactly three
      `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" pin is updated to the
      helper extraction (asserting the helper consumes the constant), so the
      duplication cannot silently return.
- [ ] **No production pacing change.** The choreography timing constants
      (`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS`, flight/stagger durations, `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS`)
      and the cap value are unchanged — pinned by existing/added unit tests;
      only the cap's enforcement mechanism differs.
- [ ] **Wait-budget guard still green.** `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`
      passes unchanged: the end-of-turn wait keeps its cap-derived 40 000 ms
      budget and `budget + 20 s boot ≤ 60 s` headroom rule. If the soak shows
      the budget can now be reduced, that reduction is a *derived* margin
      change proved by the soak, not a hand-picked literal.
- [ ] **Reliability proven, not assumed.** `/skill:test --type soak-load`
      (≥ `nproc` burners) passes with the change, and the pre-change failure at
      the same burner count is reproduced and recorded on this item; both
      before/after tables (burners, peak load, runs, wall times, summary paths)
      are posted as a comment.
- [ ] **Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/testing.md` "Measured envelope" and
      the headroom rule section record the decision (cap enforced on wall
      clock, hidden-tab semantics) and the post-fix envelope, replacing the
      "above ~2× is outside the envelope" caveat with measured evidence; the
      helper's module comment documents the wall-clock contract. All related
      documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
      README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes
      (`/skill:test --type full`), evidence recorded on this item.

## Constraints

- **No behavioural change to production pacing.** The choreography, the
  incident hold and the cap value are shipped features
  (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ, CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q); only the cap's enforcement may
  change.
- The parent's headroom constraint stands: `budget + scene-boot allowance` must
  stay inside the browser 60 s hook.
- Reduced motion must not become the sole remedy (parent decision); the
  deferred-income path keeps explicit coverage.
- All five deferral sites must keep identical semantics after extraction, and
  the existing fake-clock unit suites must not be weakened to accommodate the
  change.
- A stale wall timer must never fire into a destroyed scene — reuse the
  existing `scene.isActive()` / try-catch defensive pattern from the deferred
  closing tail.
- Agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill only
  (`/skill:test --type soak-load`, `--type full`); no ad-hoc `npx vitest` loops.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` — add the shared
  wall-clock deferral helper (sibling to `scheduleOrRun` ~line 176); adopt it in
  `finish`'s income wait (~254) and the reveal gating (~301).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — three deferral sites
  (`advanceTurn` ~433, forced event-choice ~617, piggyback ~783) adopt the
  helper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` — `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`
  unchanged; comment updated to state the wall-clock enforcement contract.
- `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` — the "exactly three
  `s.time.now + cap` sites" regex pin moves to the helper extraction.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts` — fake `time` stubs: drive the injected
  timer/clock.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` — Enter test and its
  40 000 ms margin expected unchanged.
- `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` — headroom rule re-check (expected
  unchanged).
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — "Measured envelope" + headroom rule: record the
  decision and the post-fix soak evidence.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the clamped-delta mechanism is the dominant starvation link
  and the deferral's poll cadence is the part that can be fixed without touching
  pacing. Verified against the installed Phaser source
  (`TimeStep.smoothDelta`, `Clock.now` / `Clock.elapsed` semantics); the
  before/after `soak-load` run is the confirmation.
- **Risk:** removing the late-detection link may not be sufficient on its own —
  the choreography phases before/after the deferral still stretch under
  clamped delta. Mitigation: the soak is a hard AC; if it still fails, the
  fallback is option B's separate deferral-contract test (not option D), and
  the residual envelope is re-documented with evidence.
- **Risk (accepted, decided):** a wall-clock cap changes hidden/backgrounded-tab
  behaviour — the day start is now forced after the cap instead of stalling
  until the tab paints again (Q2 = 1). This is the intended semantics of a stall
  bound; documented in the module comment and `docs/dev/testing.md`.
- **Risk:** a wall timer outliving the scene could fire into a destroyed scene.
  Mitigation: `scene.isActive()` guard plus the existing try-catch pattern; a
  unit test covers the destroyed/stale case.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the attractor is "rework all game-time animation off
  clamped delta" (tweens, phase gaps, incident hold). Explicitly out of scope —
  record as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- MS-0MVMKEU2000639TG — this item (`discovered-from:` the soak child
  MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L; soak evidence and envelope recorded there and in
  `docs/dev/testing.md` "Measured envelope").
- MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — parent: made the file's waits load-tolerant via
  cap-derived budgets; its headroom AC and "Measured limit (triaged, not a
  flake)" section are the origin of this item.
- MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L — the 20-run / under-load soak whose evidence defines the
  envelope and whose `soak-load` profile proves this fix.
- MS-0MVLINWV10005H2P — the wait-budget guard and headroom rule this item must
  keep green.
- MS-0MUYFX7Q2004JQ5R — shared end-of-turn closing presentation primitive that
  carries `incomeCollectionCapMs`.
- CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ / CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q — phased income choreography and
  deferred income window (untouched pacing; the property the cap protects).
- MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (open) — planned End-of-Turn summary dialog on the
  closing completion path; it will interact with the deferral this item
  extracts, so check dependency direction during planning.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L** – Prove browser-wait reliability: 20-run soak plus under-load run (completed)
- **MS-0MVLINWV10005H2P** – Guard browser wait budgets against production caps (completed)
- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary… (open; planned dialog on the closing path)

### Related repository files
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — engine developer guide; frame-loop/delta context.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — measured envelope and headroom rule this item updates.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — documents reduced motion, deferral pacing and
  presentation behaviour these waits must respect.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Given the measured envelope (the gate fails only above ≈2× CPU
  oversubscription, load ≥ ~31), which remediation should this item
  implement — (A) accept and document the envelope with no code change,
  (B) convert the Enter test to reduced motion plus a separate cheap
  deferral-contract test, (C) make the income-collection deferral cap
  starvation-proof (wall-clock deadline + wall-clock poll, one extracted
  helper, production change confined to the safety cap), or (D) raise the
  browser hook for this test (parent AC amendment needed)?"
  — Answer (producer): **C** — make the income-collection deferral cap
  starvation-proof. Source: interactive reply (intake interview round 1,
  2026-10-25). Agent recommendation was C (stated with rationale before the
  answer); A was recorded as the zero-production-change fallback and B's second
  variant as the fallback if C's soak still fails. Research behind the
  recommendation: Phaser `TimeStep.smoothDelta` clamps per-frame delta to
  `1000/fps.min` (200 ms default), so under rAF starvation the choreography and
  the deferral's 250 ms `delayedCall` re-polls both run at a fraction of
  wall-clock speed — the wall-clock cap deadline is therefore detected late,
  which is the link C removes.
- Q2 (conditional on C): "Should the 16 000 ms cap be enforced against wall
  clock even when the page is not painting/visible (backgrounded tab or fully
  starved rAF — the day start is forced after 16 s wall even though the
  choreography never ran), or should the forced advance hold while the document
  is hidden/blurred and resume on visibility change?"
  — Answer (producer): **as recommended** = enforce on wall clock (option 1):
  the cap is a stall bound, nothing is visible while hidden, and today a hidden
  tab already stalls the animator indefinitely. Source: interactive reply
  (intake interview round 1, 2026-10-25). Recorded as an accepted, documented
  semantic change in the Risks section and to be reflected in the helper's
  module comment and `docs/dev/testing.md`.

# Wire Bank Loan button into the Turn Summary dialog

Follow-up raised by the Bank Loans planning session (MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG), per producer
decision Q4: the Turn Summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) has landed, so its deliberately
disabled **Bank Loan** affordance can now be wired to the loan feature.

## Problem statement

The Turn Summary dialog shows an always-disabled **[ Bank Loan ]** button and never calls
the `onBankLoanAction` seam reserved for the loans feature, so a mid-game player has no
entry point to credit at all — the loan engine only surfaces offers on bankruptcy. This item
turns the reserved affordance into a working mid-game loan entry point, with no new engine
rules.

## Users

- **Mid-game human player (single-player)** — "When the Turn Summary dialog is on screen
  and I am short of cash, I want to borrow from the configured loan menu so I can fund the
  next week's move, and I want to see the repayment schedule before I commit."
- **Cautious player** — "I want the button to tell me *why* it is unavailable (loans turned
  off, or I already owe money) instead of a generic 'coming soon' note."

Not a user of this slice: competitive seats (per-seat closing text, no summary dialog),
AI seats (bailout-only policy — no proactive loans).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Enabled/disabled matrix.** The Bank Loan button is interactive only when
   `state.config.loansEnabled === true` **and** the acting (human) seat holds no active loan;
   in every other case it is rendered disabled (muted, `input` disabled) with a hint that
   explains the reason.
2. **Selector with schedule.** Pressing the enabled button opens the loan selector listing
   every configured `config.loanOptions` entry with its per-turn repayment and total
   repayment, plus a way to back out; backing out returns to the Turn Summary dialog with no
   state change.
3. **Confirm dispatches `takeLoan`.** Confirming an option dispatches the `takeLoan` command
   for the acting seat, credits the principal to that seat's wallet, records the active loan,
   and leaves `actionsRemaining` unchanged.
4. **No day advance.** Neither opening the selector nor confirming a loan advances the day or
   resumes the deferred closing; the day advances only on **[ Next Turn ]**, exactly once.
5. **Refreshed dialog.** After the loan is taken the Turn Summary dialog is re-rendered from
   the same `TurnResult` with the post-`takeLoan` state, so the new obligation is visible and
   the button is now disabled (one-active-loan rule) while **[ Next Turn ]** still works.
6. **Testing/validation.** Tests cover the enabled/disabled matrix (loans enabled + no loan,
   active loan, `loansEnabled: false`), the selector content, the `takeLoan` dispatch, the
   no-action-point rule, the cancel path, and that the day does not advance before
   **[ Next Turn ]**.
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments (`showTurnSummaryDialog`, the gate, the button-construction site),
   `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (the "[ Bank Loan ] is always disabled" paragraph), and the
   in-game help/loan documentation touched by MS-0MVPWSFDN000QJXB.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn,
  onBankLoanAction?)` renders `[ Bank Loan ]` with `disableInteractive()`, colour
  `#6b6459`, and the hint *“Bank loans are not available yet — coming in a future update.”*;
  it explicitly does `void onBankLoanAction` so the seam can never fire. `BANK_LOAN_HINT` is
  duplicated in `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts`, whose AC4 asserts
  "always disabled, seam never invoked" — that test must be rewritten, not deleted.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn,
  onBankLoanAction?)` delegates to `msOverlayManager`; with no overlay manager (headless) it
  calls `onNextTurn()` immediately so the closing is never stranded.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `shouldGateTurnSummary()` restricts the
  dialog to `requiresDeferredClosing` single-player closings (never replay, reduced motion,
  tutorial or competitive); `presentTurnSummaryGate()` builds the summary with
  `buildTurnSummary(s.state, result)` and calls
  `s.showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn)` — the third argument is not passed today.
- Overlays already read live state (`s.state.config` in `MainStreetOverlayContent`), so
  `loansEnabled` needs no new plumbing into the scene.
- `buildTurnSummary()` is Phaser-free and read-only, so re-rendering after a loan only needs
  the same `state` + `result` pair re-run.
- **The loan engine has SHIPPED** (updated at plan time, 2026-11-01). The Bank Loans epic
  MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG and all 11 of its slices are `completed`, so the dependency edge is
  satisfied and this item is unblocked. Available to build on: `src/MainStreetLoans.ts`
  (`optionsFor`, `activeLoanFor`, `canTakeLoan`, `formatLoanObligation`,
  `buildActiveLoan`, `loanTotalRepayment`, `loanPerTurnRepayment`),
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` + `MainStreetLoanOverlayModel.ts` (bailout dialog),
  `takeLoan` / `acceptLoanOffer` in `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`, `takeLoanCommand` in
  `src/MainStreetCommands.ts`, and `config.loansEnabled` / `config.loanOptions`.
- **BLOCKER found at plan time: `canTakeLoan()` refuses the dialog's dispatch.**
  `canTakeLoan()` requires `state.phase === 'MarketPhase'`, but `presentTurnSummaryGate()`
  runs *before* `advanceTurn` → `finishDeferredTurnClosing()`, and `processEndOfTurn()` has
  already left the state in `IncidentPhase` (`MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts:693`). A
  `takeLoan` dispatched from the dialog is therefore rejected with *"Loans can only be taken
  during the market phase, not IncidentPhase."* Producer decision **Q7 = A** (2026-11-01)
  authorises relaxing **only** the phase precondition for this window, which is why the
  original "presentation wiring only" constraint below is amended. Tracked by
  MS-0MVXYCIU00053HL1.
- **Repayment timing needs no change** (Assumption A1 now confirmed by code): the
  `LoanRepayment` pass runs inside the closing at `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts:725`,
  before the dialog appears, so a loan taken at the dialog first repays on the *next* turn's
  closing automatically.
- Save schema v3 (loans + pending offer) is delivered by the epic; this slice must not touch
  serialisation.

## Desired change

1. **Carry a loans descriptor into the dialog.** Extend the gate's call so the dialog receives
   one small Phaser-free descriptor rather than reaching into scene state ad hoc — predicted
   shape `{ enabled: boolean; activeLoan: { perTurnRepayment, turnsRemaining } | null;
   options: LoanOption[] }` built in `presentTurnSummaryGate()` from `s.state.config` and the
   acting seat. Keeps the overlay presentation-only and the descriptor unit-testable.
   (Implementation may instead read `s.state` directly if the epic's helpers make that
   cleaner — the ACs do not care which; see Assumptions.)
2. **Enable the affordance** when `enabled && activeLoan === null`, wiring `pointerdown` to
   the `onBankLoanAction` seam; keep the button disabled otherwise with a reason-specific
   hint (loans disabled vs. already owing — see open question Q3).
3. **Loan selector** presented on press: reuse the epic's `MainStreetLoanOverlay` option rows
   (per-turn + total repayment). The epic builds it for a *pending offer* driven by
   `state.pendingLoanOffer`; this slice needs a non-bailout mode (no pending offer, options
   from `config.loanOptions`, Cancel/back instead of Decline). Reusing the row renderer, not
   duplicating it, is the requirement; a small `mode` parameter is expected.
4. **Confirm = dispatch.** Confirming dispatches the `takeLoan` command through the existing
   command surface (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts`), never mutating state inline.
5. **Refresh in place** after a successful take: rebuild the summary from the same
   `TurnResult` and re-render the dialog (dismiss the old overlay objects first so
   `s.overlayObjects` stays consistent), leaving `[ Next Turn ]` as the only way to resume
   `advanceTurn`.
6. **Tests** in a new `tests/main-street/turn-summary-bank-loan.browser.test.ts` (browser
   overlay, mirroring `turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` helpers) plus the rewrite of the
   dialog suite's AC4 case.

## Constraints

- **Presentation wiring only, with one authorised exception (Q7 = A).** No changes to the
  loan model, repayment maths or the one-active-loan validation — those belong to
  MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG and stay untouched. The single permitted engine change is relaxing
  `canTakeLoan()`'s `MarketPhase` precondition for the seat's own deferred-closing window,
  behind an explicit opt-in, so the dialog's dispatch is not refused (see "Existing state").
- **No action point cost** and **no day advance** — taking a loan from the dialog must leave
  `actionsRemaining` untouched and must not resume the deferred closing.
- **Single-player deferred path only** — the dialog itself is gated to that path; competitive
  per-seat closing and the tutorial/reduced-motion/replay paths are unchanged.
- **Overlay conventions** (`core` UI best practices): `createOverlayBackground` +
  `createOverlayButton`, all elements parented into `s.hudContainer` and pushed to
  `s.overlayObjects`, depths 199/200/201, instant appearance (reduced-motion safe), SFX via
  `safePlaySound`.
- **Dependency now satisfied** — depended on MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (dependency edge already
  recorded): specifically the loan model/config slice (MS-0MVPWS5JB007YSHB), the `takeLoan`
  command slice (MS-0MVPWS6WB008WP79) and the overlay-UI slice (MS-0MVPWSBLG006YMBA).

## Assumptions

- **A1 First repayment falls on the next turn's closing.** The closing sequence (and its
  ledger) has already run when the dialog is presented, so a loan taken at the dialog must not
  charge a repayment against the turn being summarised. **Confirmed at plan time by the
  shipped code** — the `LoanRepayment` pass runs inside the closing
  (`MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts:725`) before the dialog is presented, so Q1 is resolved as
  A with no engine change.
- **A2 Proactive loans are allowed at any coin balance** — the button is not gated on

# tce-main-street dev builds re-pin the engine when it advances, invalidating the test cache and pushing the full suite past `timeoutPerCommand`

**Headline:** When the engine `dev` tip has advanced past the pinned SHA, `npm run build` re-pins the engine and stages `configs/engine-pin.json` + the `core` gitlink, so the finish gate re-runs the full suite against a *dirty* tree that can exceed `timeoutPerCommand` on a loaded host. Producer decisions are recorded: this repo owns the immediate unblock (timeout + guard + docs); the finish-gate composition exclusion and the vitest/`suiteCommands` changed-scope fixes land in **SorraAgents** and are cross-referenced here.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` runs **build → test → commit** in a worktree. The build runs `npm run build`, whose first step is `npm run engine:sync`. When the engine's tracked branch tip has advanced beyond a worktree's committed pin, `engine:sync` runs `git submodule update --remote core`, rewrites `configs/engine-pin.json` and **stages the pin and the `core` gitlink** (`core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs`, `stageEngineState`). The test gate then evaluates a tree that is dirty *because of the build*, and the cache key (`skill/test_cache.py:compute_git_state` — `HEAD` plus the content of every dirty path) no longer matches any pre-warmed green entry. On the shared host the resulting full-suite run measured **2846 s**, above `timeoutPerCommand: 1800`, and the gate failed with `Test run 1/3 failed (unknown)`, `failures: []` — a kill/unparsed failure presented as a code failure.

Two independent defects compound it:

1. **`changed-scope` is silently disabled for this repo.** `changed_scope_commands()` returns `None` immediately when `.pi/test-config.json` declares `suiteCommands` (the documented fast path is unavailable here), and even without that guard `map_changed_to_tests()` only understands pytest and `*.test.mjs` node tests — it has no vitest/`.test.ts` mapping. `implement.py finish` therefore warns `changed-scope selection unavailable … falling back to full scope` and every finish, including docs/evidence-only items, pays the full suite (reproduced twice; `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-finish.log` line 4).
2. **Queue time is indistinguishable from test time, and a kill is indistinguishable from a failure.** The host-wide test semaphore (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2`) is shared by all repos; measured slot waits of 1040–2400 s appeared as `slot_busy`, and a non-zero/killed run with no parsable failures reported `reason: unknown`. `timeoutPerCommand` bounds the whole command, and the documented remediation ("set it high enough to cover the full suite with headroom") is currently 1800 against a measured 2846 s.

## Producer decisions (resolved)

All three decisions were made by the producer in-session (source: interactive reply `A / A / A`, recorded in the Appendix). They fix the scope and design:

- **Q1 = A — scope and home.** This MS item owns the requirements, evidence and the **repo-local** `.pi/test-config.json` timeout/docs mitigation. The framework behaviour fixes are filed in **SorraAgents** and cross-referenced here (precedent: `MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57` → `SA-0MVO274QN006GXGQ`). This item is **not** an epic and remains a `bug`; the SA items are tracked in SorraAgents and cross-referenced here.
- **Q2 = A — engine re-pin remedy.** The finish gate must not commit or test build-artefact churn it did not originate: exclude the `core` gitlink and `configs/engine-pin.json` from the finish commit unless the item itself changed the engine composition, and prove that the tested composition equals the committed composition. Do **not** relax the cache key (remedy B rejected) and do **not** change `engine:sync` to verify-only (remedy C rejected).
- **Q3 = A — changed-scope approach.** Add a vitest/TS-aware selection and honour declared `groups` even when `suiteCommands` is present. `suiteCommands` defines the **full** suite only; it must no longer disable selection.

## Users

- **Implement agent (primary) — user story:** "As an implement agent finishing a work item, I need the finish gate to test the engine composition that will actually be committed, and to reuse a valid green cache entry, so a documentation- or evidence-only item is not blocked by a 47-minute unrelated engine suite."
- **Implement agent — user story:** "When the gate fails, I need to know whether it was a code failure, a suite timeout, or a test-slot wait, so I fix the right thing instead of retrying blindly."
- **Repo maintainer — user story:** "As the maintainer, I want an engine bump to be a deliberate, reviewable change, not a side effect silently swept into every documentation commit."
- **Release operator — user story:** "I need the pin and the `core` gitlink to remain coherent, so the release pin-contract gate stays trustworthy."

## Acceptance Criteria

Each AC names the repo that owns it. AC1–AC3 are satisfied by the cross-referenced SorraAgents items; AC4–AC5 land here.

- [ ] **AC1 — no build-artefact churn in the tested/committed tree (SorraAgents, Q2=A).** With a worktree created from a commit whose `configs/engine-pin.json` lags the engine tracked tip, `implement.py finish` on a source-unchanged item does **not** let `npm run build`'s `engine:sync` re-pin or gitlink advance become part of the item's commit. The tested composition equals the committed composition (the pin in `HEAD`), and the gate verdict records the composed engine SHA plus whether the suite ran or was cache-served. The test cache key is unchanged (remedy B rejected). Proven by a git-fixture test with a submodule whose checkout HEAD differs from the recorded gitlink, plus a live run on this repo.
- [ ] **AC2 — `changed-scope` works for this repo (SorraAgents, Q3=A).** For a change set covered by a declared `groups` entry or by a changed vitest test file, `implement.py finish` runs the targeted selection and reports `scope: changed` with the selected commands; declaring `suiteCommands` no longer disables selection, and `suiteCommands` continues to define only the full suite. When no safe subset exists, the fallback names the specific reason (e.g. "no changed source/test files", "no matching group") instead of a generic list. Proven by selector unit tests (vitest/TS + `suiteCommands` + groups) and a live finish log showing `scope: changed`.
- [ ] **AC3 — timeout and queue failures are self-describing (SorraAgents, coordinated with `SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI`).** A suite that exceeds `timeoutPerCommand`, or is killed without parsable failures, is reported as an infrastructure/timeout condition (never `reason: unknown` with `failures: []`), including the configured timeout, elapsed time, and — separately — the semaphore queue wait. Queue wait is not charged to the suite's per-command timeout, or is reported as its own `slot_busy` duration. Proven by gate-classification unit tests and a simulated timeout/kill fixture.
- [ ] **AC4 — honest, bounded timeout configuration and documentation (this repo).** `timeoutPerCommand` is set from measured evidence to cover the loaded-host full suite with headroom (measured 2846 s → set 3600 s; confirm whether it is per command or per suite first), and a guard test fails if it is lowered below the documented measured worst case plus headroom. `docs/dev/testing.md` and `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` record the measured values, the per-command/queue semantics, the engine composition at finish, and the remediation; framework docs (`implement/SKILL.md`, the test skill reference) are updated where the SA behaviour changes.
- [ ] **AC5 — validation and full suite.** Reproduced and pinned by a test at each module under change; all related documentation is updated (including code comments and README where relevant); the full project test suite passes with the new changes (framework node/pytest suites for SorraAgents changes; this repo's suite for repo-local changes).

## Constraints

- **Pin policy is preserved.** `CG-0MVO268500071BPI` requires the pin to track the engine `dev` tip and the pin + gitlink to travel together in one commit. Q2=A does not stop `engine:sync` from running on dev builds; it only prevents the **finish gate** from sweeping that build-originated churn into an item's commit. Any further deviation needs producer sign-off.
- **Repository boundaries.** This repo must not edit `.pi/` or the agent framework in `~/.pi/agent/skills` directly; framework fixes land in **SorraAgents** and are cross-referenced (Q1=A). The engine-sync script remains canonical in **Tableau-Card-Engine** and is **not** changed (Q2 ≠ C).
- **Cache correctness over speed.** The cache key is not relaxed (Q2 ≠ B); a green entry recorded on a different engine must never satisfy the gate (see `SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L`).
- **Test execution policy.** Validation runs go through `/skill:test`; no ad-hoc suites. The host test semaphore must not be bypassed.
- **`timeoutPerCommand` is shared.** `implement.py` also uses it as the `git push` timeout, so raising it widens the push window too.
- **Language.** UK English throughout.

## Existing state
- **AC4 landed (2026-10-29, released in v0.1.23).** The repo-local half of this item is done: `timeoutPerCommand` is 3600 s (measured 2846.6 s + ~26 % headroom) with a guard test, and `docs/dev/testing.md` + `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` document the finish-gate composition, cache, timeout and queue-wait semantics. Children `MS-0MVTEVJBH003GE8W` and `MS-0MVTEVJRX005N0EA` are closed; `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1` (AC5) stays blocked behind the AC1–AC3 verification children.

- `configs/engine-pin.json` and the `core` gitlink are currently coherent at `f5c0a1b1` (= local `core` HEAD = `origin/dev` tip), so the main checkout is clean; the failure requires a lagging pin (a worktree from an older commit or an engine advance after the worktree was created).
- Evidence (read-only, outside the repo):
  - `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-finish.log` — `engine:sync: core updated 0409c1eb5f → 19f30ac713`, pin staged; gate result `success: false`, `notices: []`, `reason: unknown`, `phase_finish` 2215 s.
  - `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-full.log` — green full suite, `elapsed: 2846.6 s`.
  - `/tmp/ms0mvpy2ydq-finish.log` — `reason: slot_contention`, slot wait 2400 s.
  - `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-warm3.log` — `slot_busy` after 1500 s.
- Current config: `.pi/test-config.json` `timeoutPerCommand: 3600` (raised from 1800 by AC4; shipped in v0.1.23), `suiteCommands` = 3 commands (`npm --silent test`, MainStreetScene browser, e2e no-console-errors), plus 11 named `groups`; the timeout floor and the group/suite shape are guarded by `tests/tooling/test-config-timeout-guard.test.ts`.
- Existing guards: engine checkout preflight (`tests/tooling/engine-checkout-precheck.ts`, `MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV`) fails loudly when `./core` is behind the pin; `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` holds the release pin contract.

Extends `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2` / `SA-0MVQHVGFR006W8LG` rather than duplicating them.
   - **SA-item B — changed-scope for `suiteCommands` + vitest/TS.** Honour declared `groups` and add a vitest/TS selection; `suiteCommands` defines the full suite only. Builds on `SA-0MUJKF2HP001BR51`.
   - **SA-item C — timeout/queue classification.** Distinguish timeout/kill from unparsed failure, report timeout + elapsed + queue wait separately, and keep queue wait out of the per-command timeout. Coordinate with `SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI` (slot fairness) and `SA-0MUKHCO02009EQFG` (pacer).
3. **Engine repo (Tableau-Card-Engine):** no change — verify-only sync (remedy C) rejected.

# Verification: remote pack discovery, integrity & degradation

## Goal

Prove — with automated tests — that a remote pack catalogue is discovered,
cryptographically verified, and safely degraded when anything goes wrong, so
the parent's discovery, degradation, rejection and integrity criteria are
met by evidence rather than assertion.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 1, 3, 4 and 6).

## Scope

Verification-only: this item adds or hardens tests and fixtures; it does not
add production behaviour. Where a test exposes a real gap in the remote
source, record the gap and raise a comment on the sibling feature item rather
than implementing the fix here.

Coverage to establish:

1. **Discovery.** A pack catalogue served from a configured host appears in
   the discovery result alongside bundled packs, with its manifest, cards CSV
   and pack id intact.
2. **Signature gate.** A valid signature loads; missing, invalid, wrong-key,
   and malformed-envelope manifests each reject the source **whole** (every
   path from that source resolves `null`) with exactly one warning.
3. **Degradation.** Unreachable host, connection rejection, HTTP error,
   slow/hung host (bounded timeout), and malformed manifest JSON each leave
   boot on bundled content, never throw, and never leave the Card Packs
   listing empty when a bundled pack exists.
4. **Rejection of bad data.** A pack whose CSV header is wrong, or whose card
   ids duplicate an already-accepted pack, is rejected by the existing core
   merge without affecting packs from other sources.

Tests must use an injected fake `fetch`/transport and injected timers so the
suite never performs real network I/O and never waits a real 3 seconds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Remote discovery is covered: a signed remote pack served by a fake
      transport appears in `loadMainStreetCardPacks`' result with its cards
      merged into the pool.
- [ ] Every signature failure mode is covered: missing signature, invalid
      signature, signature from a non-pinned key, and malformed envelope each
      reject the whole source and emit exactly one warning.
- [ ] Every degradation mode is covered: unreachable host, rejected fetch,
      non-2xx response, timeout abort, and unparseable manifest each boot on
      bundled content with no throw.
- [ ] A test asserts the timeout is bounded at the configured value using fake
      timers — no test waits on a real clock.
- [ ] A test asserts the Card Packs listing input is non-empty when a bundled
      pack exists and the remote source fails.
- [ ] Bad pack data (wrong header, duplicate card ids) is covered as rejected
      whole without affecting sibling sources.
- [ ] No test performs real network I/O; every fetch goes through an injected
      transport.
- [ ] Changed-scope tests pass through the test skill.

# Verification: remote pack precedence, gating & asset parity

## Goal

Prove that remote packs are indistinguishable from bundled packs at the
registry, gating and asset layers, and that precedence is deterministic, so the
parent's parity, precedence and asset-resolution criteria are evidenced by
automated tests.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 2, 5 and 7).

## Scope

Verification-only: this item adds tests and fixtures; it does not add
production behaviour. Gaps found are reported on the sibling feature items.

Coverage to establish:

1. **Precedence — bundled wins.** A pack id present in both the bundled and a
   remote source is served from the bundled source, byte-for-byte.
2. **Precedence — remote first-wins.** Two remote sources carrying the same
   pack id resolve to the first-registered source's content.
3. **Registry composition.** The composed registry order is bundled first,
   then remote sources in configured URL order; registration is idempotent by
   id and never reorders existing sources.
4. **Gating parity.** An entitled remote pack is loaded; an unentitled remote
   pack is `locked` and contributes no rows; the scoped simulated purchase
   promotes the declared remote pack and re-discovers it — the same flow as
   the bundled residential pack.
5. **Persistence parity.** A save created with a remote pack active restores
   the same active pack set and merged checksum after a load round-trip.
6. **Asset parity.** A remote pack's `assetUrls` entries resolve to absolute
   URLs on the configured remote base, are gated on manifest verification, and
   reject traversal/undeclared asset paths.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test asserts bundled content wins over a remote source carrying the
      same pack id (byte-for-byte comparison).
- [ ] A test asserts first-wins between two remote sources in registration
      order.
- [ ] A test asserts the composed registry order is bundled → remote(s) in
      configured order, and that re-adding a source is a no-op.
- [ ] A test asserts an unentitled remote pack is reported `locked` and
      contributes no merged rows.
- [ ] A test asserts the scoped simulated purchase unlocks the declared remote
      pack and the post-purchase discovery loads it.
- [ ] A save/load round-trip test asserts the active remote pack set and merged
      checksum are preserved.
- [ ] A test asserts remote `assetUrls` resolve to the configured remote base,
      that a rejected source resolves no assets, and that undeclared or
      traversal asset paths resolve `null`.
- [ ] Changed-scope tests pass through the test skill.

# Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)

## Goal

As a distribution operator, I want a signed pack catalogue hosted at a
configured URL to be discovered at runtime and merged into the player's card
pool, so that I can publish packs without rebuilding the game; as a player I
want those packs to show up in my Card Packs panel exactly like bundled packs.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 1 and 6; parent scope items 1, 2, 6;
parent constraints "reuse existing seams", "totality", "additive", "signing key
separation"; locked decisions Q1 and Q2).

## Context

This is the tracer bullet: it cuts every layer once, end-to-end, so the whole
seam is proven before it is hardened. `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` already provides
`PackSource` / `PackSourceRegistry` and adapts a registry to the loader's
`fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` seams, so **no core loader change**
is needed. The remote source is a provider on that registry.

Without this slice there is no usable increment: a signature gate is
inseparable from discovery (an unverified catalogue must never contribute
packs), so verification lands with the first end-to-end path rather than as a
separate layer.

## Scope

1. **Configuration surface.** Read the remote catalogue coordinates from
   `import.meta.env` (`VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL`,
   `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY`), validate them, and derive the host
   allow-list. Inert when unset.
2. **Allow-listed bounded fetch primitive.** One total text-fetch helper: refuse
   a host that is not configured (before any request), enforce a hard timeout
   via `AbortController`, map every failure to `null` + one warning.
3. **Signed-manifest verification.** The signed envelope, its deterministic
   canonical payload bytes, pinned-key import from raw base64, and a total
   verifier returning a discriminated result (never throws).
4. **Remote pack source.** `createRemotePackSource(config)` serving
   `<base>/packs/manifest.json` and `<base>/packs/<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv`
   after verification, rejecting the **whole source** on any verification or
   manifest-shape failure.
5. **Composition and boot wiring.** Compose the registry as bundled source
   first, then the remote source; use it on the browser boot path
   (`bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks`) without touching the Electron
   content-directory path.

## Design notes

- Ed25519 is available natively in Node 22 WebCrypto and the Playwright
  Chromium used by the browser project — **no new runtime dependency**.
- Verification is memoised per source instance: one manifest fetch and one
  verification per boot, not one per CSV.
- The source's remit is "fetch and refuse only". Merging, precedence and
  duplicate-id rejection stay with the registry and the core merge, which is
  what makes bundled/remote parity automatic.
- Every failure is a warning on the existing logger seam; no UI change
  (decision Q3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Remote discovery.** A pack catalogue hosted at a configured (build-time)
- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Signed-manifest integrity.** A remote manifest whose Ed25519 signature is
- [ ] `src/MainStreetRemotePackConfig.ts` parses and validates `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` and `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY` (injectable env for tests) and exposes an allow-list predicate; unset, blank or invalid configuration yields no remote sources and logs a warning rather than throwing.
- [ ] `src/MainStreetRemotePackManifest.ts` exports the signed envelope type and a deterministic canonical-payload function, plus `verifyPackManifestSignature(...)` returning `ok` / `missing-signature` / `invalid-signature` / `malformed-envelope` / `unavailable` and never throwing for any input.
- [ ] A manifest signed with the matching private key verifies `ok`; a one-byte body change or a signature from a different keypair returns `invalid-signature`; a blank or absent signature returns `missing-signature`; a non-JSON or wrong-shape envelope returns `malformed-envelope`.
- [ ] The canonical payload is stable under input key reordering so an external operator can reproduce the signed bytes; asserted by a test.
- [ ] A total fetched-text helper refuses a non-configured host **without calling the injected `fetch`**, and maps timeout, rejection, non-2xx and body-read failure to `null` with one warning.
- [ ] A `createRemotePackSource(config)` factory returns a `PackSource` whose `id` distinguishes it from the bundled source, serving `manifest.json` and `<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv` from the configured base once the manifest verifies.
- [ ] A remote pack served by a fake transport appears in `loadMainStreetCardPacks` merged pool with its cards and reaches the Card Packs listing input; asserted by a test.

- [ ] `bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks` composes the configured remote source on the browser path, while an explicit launcher `contentDir` composes no remote source and performs no remote fetch (asserted with a spy).

# Remote pack degradation & bounded timeout hardening

## Goal

As a player, I want the game to always start and play on bundled packs when the
remote host is slow, hung, unreachable or serving rubbish, so that remote
hosting can never block boot or leave me with an empty Card Packs panel.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 3 and 4; parent scope items 5 and 7;
parent constraint "bounded timeout"; locked decision Q3).

## Context

The tracer bullet proves the happy path. This slice hardens the failure paths,
which is where the parent's risk register concentrates (boot latency, offline
regression). All of it is end-to-end observable: the game boots, bundled cards
deal, the listing is non-empty, and the console shows exactly one actionable
warning per rejected source.

## Scope

- Enforce the hard ≈3 s timeout on **every** remote request (manifest and each
  pack CSV), with the abort timer always cleared so no handle leaks.
- Degrade to bundled content — never throw, never blank the listing — for:
  unreachable host, connection rejection, non-2xx status, timeout abort,
  unparseable manifest JSON, wrong manifest schema/version, and a manifest
  entry with no readable `cards` file.
- Per-pack isolation: one unreadable CSV degrades only that pack, so other
  packs from the same source still load.
- Explicit "no client-side caching" behaviour: the source writes nothing to
  `localStorage` / Cache Storage and re-fetches on each boot.
- Warning quality: one warning per rejected source and one per failed pack,
  naming the source/pack and the reason.

## Design notes

- The timeout is per request, so a hung manifest does not consume the budget of
  every CSV read.
- Tests use injected `fetch` and fake timers throughout: no real network, no
  real 3-second waits.
- The bounded-timeout default (3000 ms) is a single exported constant so the
  documentation and the tests reference one value.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Degradation.** When the remote host is unreachable, slow, or serves a
- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Rejection of bad data.** A malformed remote manifest or a pack with a bad

# Multi-source composition & deterministic precedence

## Goal

As a player, I want a remote pack to never override bundled core content, and
deterministic behaviour when two remote catalogues offer the same pack, so that
remote hosting cannot silently replace or corrupt the game's own packs.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent AC 5; parent scope items 2 and 3; parent
constraint "additive"; locked decision Q4).

## Context

`PackSourceRegistry` is first-wins by consultation order and `add()` never
reorders. Precedence is therefore *derived from composition order*. The tracer
bullet composed one remote source; this slice makes composition a first-class,
explicitly ordered function that supports several remote catalogues, and pins
the precedence guarantees with tests.

Equally important: the change must remain **inert** for the Electron
content-directory path and for an unconfigured build.

## Scope

- Compose several remote sources additively in configured URL order, always
  after the bundled source.
- Guarantee and test: bundled wins over remote (byte-for-byte); between remote
  sources the first registered wins.
- Idempotent, order-preserving composition; re-adding a duplicate source id is a
  no-op.
- Resilience: a remote source that cannot be constructed is skipped with a
  warning; bundled content still serves.
- Inertness: configuration unset, and the Electron content-directory path, both
  behave exactly as before (no remote source, no remote fetch).
- Gating is untouched — remote packs flow through the unchanged
  `composeContentUnlockEntitlement` resolver, so nothing is automatically
  ungated.

## Design notes

- Composition is a distinct, explicitly named entry point beside
  `createDefaultPackSourceRegistry`; the latter keeps its bundled-only meaning
  so existing callers and tests are unaffected.
- One place decides source order, mirroring the module's existing contract that
  "the registry is the single place source order is decided".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Deterministic precedence.** Bundled packs always win over remote packs
- [ ] A composition function (e.g. `createConfiguredPackSourceRegistry(config)`) returns a registry whose `sources` order is exactly the bundled source followed by each configured remote source in configured URL order.
- [ ] `createDefaultPackSourceRegistry()` remains bundled-only; existing registry behaviour and tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] A test asserts bundled content wins when the bundled and a remote source both carry the same pack path (byte-for-byte comparison).
- [ ] A test asserts a pack id offered by two remote sources resolves to the first-registered source content.
- [ ] Composition is idempotent: composing twice, or adding a source with a duplicate id, creates no duplicate and reorders nothing.
- [ ] A remote source that throws during construction is skipped with a warning and the bundled source still serves content.
- [ ] With configuration unset, the browser boot path yields a result identical to the bundled-only build.
- [ ] With an explicit launcher `contentDir`, no remote source is composed and no remote fetch occurs (asserted with a spy `fetch`).
- [ ] A remote pack cards reach the applied pool through `bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks` when configured.
- [ ] An unentitled remote pack is reported `locked`; no ungating shortcut is introduced.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts`
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`
- `src/createMainStreetGame.ts`
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackPrecedence.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/PackSourceRegistry.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Ordered, multi-source composition with explicit precedence guarantees.
- Tests for precedence, idempotence, resilience and inertness.

## Dependencies

- Depends on *Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)*.

# Remote pack asset resolution

## Goal

As a player, I want a remote pack's card art to render correctly, so that a
remote pack looks and plays exactly like a bundled pack.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent AC 7; parent scope item 1; related work
`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` — pack assets self-contained).

## Context

`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` made pack art travel with the pack: the loader produces
`tce-packs://` asset URLs, `resolvePackFileUrl` maps them through the registry,
and pack art is registered from `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls`. A bundled source
answers with a same-origin Vite `?url`; a remote source must answer with an
absolute URL on the configured remote base, and only for assets the verified
manifest declares.

This is a vertical slice: registry resolution → loader `assetUrls` → the pack
art registry → the rendered card texture.

## Scope

- Implement `resolvePackFileUrl(path)` on the remote source, returning
  `<base>/packs/<path>` for assets declared by the verified manifest.
- Gate resolution on successful manifest verification: a rejected source
  resolves no assets.
- Reject paths that escape the packs root (traversal) or are not declared by the
  manifest.
- Verify the resolved URL reaches `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls` and the pack art
  registry so a remote pack's art is available before textures are generated.

## Design notes

- URL joining must respect a base URL with a path component (a catalogue may be
  hosted under a prefix) and must not double or drop slashes.
- The source returns a URL only; the existing asset-byte transport performs the
  fetch, so the remote source adds no new byte-reading path.
- No caching of asset URLs across boots (consistent with "no client-side
  caching this iteration").

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Asset resolution.** Remote pack art resolves and renders correctly,
- [ ] The remote source implements `resolvePackFileUrl(path)` returning an absolute URL on the configured remote base for an asset declared by the verified manifest.
- [ ] A base URL carrying a path prefix (e.g. `https://host/packs-v2/`) is joined correctly; asserted by a test.
- [ ] A rejected source (failed signature or malformed manifest) resolves no asset URLs.
- [ ] An asset path not declared in the manifest, and a path containing `..` or a backslash traversal, resolves `null`.
- [ ] An integration test asserts a remote pack `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls` entry is the remote absolute URL and that pack art registration receives it.
- [ ] A remote pack with art renders in the browser pack path, covered by an asset-resolution assertion or a browser test.
- [ ] The source does not add a new asset byte-read path; the existing `fetchAsset` transport still performs the read.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` — `resolvePackFileUrl` on the remote source
- `src/MainStreetCardPackArt.ts` — pack art registration seam
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackAssets.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Remote asset URL resolution gated on manifest verification.
- Tests covering URL shape, prefix joining, gating and traversal rejection.

## Dependencies

- Depends on *Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)*.

# Remote pack gating & behaviour parity

## Goal

As a player, I want remote packs to lock, purchase, enable, deal and persist
exactly like bundled packs, so that hosting a pack remotely changes where it
comes from and nothing else.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 2 and 4; parent scope item 4).

## Context

Content-unlock gating is data-driven: `MAIN_STREET_CONTENT_UNLOCK_GATED_PACKS`
declares which packs are gated and `composeContentUnlockEntitlement` plugs into
the loader's `resolveEntitlement` seam. Remote packs must flow through that same
resolver unchanged — the remote source contributes *content*, never
*entitlement*. This slice proves that and covers the interactive flow end to
end.

## Scope

- Confirm an entitled remote pack loads and its cards merge; an unentitled
  remote pack is `locked` and contributes no rows.
- Confirm the scoped simulated purchase (`purchaseMainStreetCardPack`) unlocks a
  declared remote pack, re-discovers it with the same transports, and that the
  pack's cards then merge and deal.
- Confirm enable/disable parity (`applyEnabledMainStreetPacks`), including the
  refusal when a live card instance would be stranded.
- Confirm save/load round-trip parity: the active remote pack set and merged
  checksum are persisted and restored.
- Introduce no ungating shortcut: the remote source must not bypass or relax
  `resolveEntitlement`.

## Design notes

- The pack id a remote catalogue publishes is the entitlement key, exactly as
  for a bundled pack (`dlc:<gameId>:<packId>`). A remote pack that is not
  declared in the gating table keeps the default (Steam-DLC / declared-unlock)
  behaviour — it is never implicitly free.
- This slice is test-and-wiring only where the parity already holds; any real
  gap found becomes a fix here because parity is the parent's AC2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Parity.** Remote packs behave identically to bundled packs across the full
- [ ] A test asserts an entitled remote pack is loaded by `loadMainStreetCardPacks` and its cards appear in the merged pool.
- [ ] A test asserts an unentitled remote pack is reported in `locked` and contributes zero merged rows.
- [ ] A test asserts `purchaseMainStreetCardPack` unlocks a declared remote pack, re-discovers it, and returns `purchased: true`, with the pack cards merged afterwards.
- [ ] A test asserts the scoped purchase evaluates only the declared pack purchase rule (no collateral unlocks).
- [ ] A test asserts a save/load round-trip preserves the remote pack active set (id plus version) and merged checksum.
- [ ] A test asserts enabling and disabling a remote pack re-merges the pool, and that disabling is refused while one of its cards is live in state.
- [ ] A test asserts the remote source never supplies or overrides an entitlement; gating remains owned by `composeContentUnlockEntitlement`.
- [ ] The full pack flow (lock, purchase, enable, deal) is covered for a remote pack by automated tests.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`
- `src/MainStreetContentUnlockGate.ts`
- `src/MainStreetPrefs.ts`
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackGatingParity.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Gating and interactive-flow parity for remote packs, evidenced by tests.
- Gaps found in parity closed at the wiring level (never by relaxing gating).

## Dependencies

- Depends on *Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)*.
- Depends on *Multi-source composition & deterministic precedence*.

# Documentation: remote pack hosting contract

## Goal

As a distribution operator, I want a written contract for hosting a remote pack
catalogue — where the files go, how the manifest is signed, what the game does
when it cannot verify or reach the host — so that I can publish packs without
reading the source code.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent AC 8, parent scope item 8).

## Scope

- **Configuration** — `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` and `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY`,
  that they are build-time (changing a URL requires a rebuild), and that
  multiple URLs compose in order.
- **Hosting layout** — the exact URL paths the game requests:
  `<base>/packs/manifest.json`, `<base>/packs/<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv`,
  `<base>/packs/<gameId>/<packId>/assets/…`. A worked example tree is required.
- **Signing contract** — the signed envelope shape, the canonical payload bytes
  (including key ordering and whitespace rules), the algorithm (Ed25519) and
  the key separation rule: the private key is held by the operator and never
  shipped in the game. Include a worked example and the verification outcome
  table.
- **Degradation semantics** — the ≈3 s bounded timeout, console-warning-only
  degradation, bundled-wins precedence, no client-side caching, and that
  bundled packs remain the offline story.
- **Licence-clean requirement** — remote pack content must satisfy the same
  licence requirements as bundled packs.

## Design notes

- Documentation-only slice: it consumes the contract implemented by the
  sibling feature items and must not introduce new behaviour.
- The verification outcome table must match the verifier's discriminated
  results exactly (`ok` / `missing-signature` / `invalid-signature` /
  `malformed-envelope` / `unavailable`), so operators can map a console warning
  to a cause.
- Explicitly list the recorded follow-ups (signing tooling, client-side
  caching, runtime/launcher URL configuration) so operators know what is not
  in this iteration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Documentation.** README / packs README / DEPLOYMENT documentation covers
- [ ] `packs/README.md` documents the remote catalogue layout with a worked URL tree, and states that a hosted catalogue uses the same `manifest.json` shape as the bundled packs plus the signature.
- [ ] The signed-envelope shape and canonical payload rules are documented with a worked example an operator can reproduce, and every verifier failure reason is listed with its meaning.
- [ ] `./DEPLOYMENT.md` (or a linked page under `docs/`) documents `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` and `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY`, the rebuild-to-change rule, and multiple-URL ordering.
- [ ] Degradation semantics are documented: about 3 s timeout, console warning only, bundled always wins, no UI change, no client-side caching.
- [ ] The signing key separation rule is stated: the private key never ships; only the public key is pinned at build time.
- [ ] The licence-clean requirement for remote pack content is stated.
- [ ] The out-of-scope follow-ups (signing tooling, caching, runtime URL configuration) are recorded as follow-ups, not documented as available.
- [ ] Existing documentation tests still pass and the new sections are reachable from the README.

## Key Files

- `packs/README.md`
- `./DEPLOYMENT.md`
- `./README.md`
- `docs/index.md`

## Deliverables

- The hosting contract documentation for distribution operators.
- A verification-outcome table mapping warnings to causes.

## Dependencies

- Depends on *Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)*.
- Depends on *Multi-source composition & deterministic precedence*.
- Depends on *Remote pack asset resolution*.

Parent: MS-0MVPWSQMG004198C (Wire Bank Loan button into Turn Summary dialog).

## Goal

Make confirming a selector option actually take the loan through the command
surface, then refresh the Turn Summary dialog in place from the same
`TurnResult` so the new obligation is visible — without spending an action or
advancing the day.

## Context

- `takeLoanCommand(state, optionIndex)` in `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` (line
  ~792) is the AP-neutral, reversible command wrapping the engine's
  `takeLoan()`; it snapshots the active-loan record, pending offer and credited
  resources.
- `buildTurnSummary(state, result)` is Phaser-free and read-only, so
  re-rendering after a take only needs the same `state` + `result` pair re-run.
- The deferred closing has already run its ledger and the `LoanRepayment` pass
  by the time the dialog appears, so a loan taken here first repays next turn.
- Overlay dismissal must reset `s.overlayObjects` the same way
  `dismissOverlay()` does, or duplicated buttons accumulate in
  `hudContainer`.

## Desired change

1. On confirm, dispatch `takeLoanCommand(s.state, optionIndex)` with the
   closing-window opt-in from slice -4 — never mutate state inline.
2. On success: rebuild the summary via `buildTurnSummary(s.state, result)` with
   the **same** `result` object and re-render the dialog (dismiss the old
   overlay objects first so `s.overlayObjects` stays consistent).
3. On refusal: show the engine's reason inside the dialog and keep it open.
4. Leave `[ Next Turn ]` as the only way to resume `advanceTurn`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Confirming an option dispatches `takeLoanCommand` for the acting seat: the principal is credited to that seat's wallet and the active loan is recorded in `state.loans`.
- `actionsRemaining` and `bankedActions` are unchanged by the take.
- The day does not advance: `state.turn` is unchanged and the deferred closing is not resumed by opening the selector, confirming, or cancelling — it advances exactly once, on `[ Next Turn ]`.
- After a successful take the dialog is re-rendered from the same `TurnResult` with the post-take state: the button is now disabled with the outstanding-obligation hint, and `[ Next Turn ]` still resumes the closing.
- The refreshed dialog leaves exactly one `[ Next Turn ]` and one `[ Bank Loan ]` button in `s.overlayObjects` / `hudContainer` (no overlay-object leak).
- An engine refusal (e.g. a race into an active loan) is surfaced as the engine's reason in the dialog, which stays open, with no state change.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-bank-loan.browser.test.ts` covers the dispatch, the no-action-point rule, the no-day-advance rule, the refresh, the leak check and the refusal path.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — confirm dispatch + in-place refresh
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `takeLoanCommand` closing-window opt-in (from slice -4)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — read-only reuse of `buildTurnSummary`
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-bank-loan.browser.test.ts` — dispatch/refresh/refusal tests

## Summary

Parent MS-0MVMKEU2000639TG (decision C, implemented in MS-0MVPY2ZM70055N2X)
replaced five duplicated scene-clock deferral polls with one wall-clock
`deferUntilIncomeCollected` helper. The unit contract tests prove the cap is

deliberately scene-clock paced (parent AC5 forbids pacing changes), so under

- `tests/main-street/bounded-deferral.test.ts` — extend with the

- [ ] `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` passes with the re-derived

## Observation

`run_tests.py --scope changed` resolves the touched paths to **one** named group from `.pi/test-config.json` using `select_group_from_changed_files()`: every matching group is scored by `len(spec['commands'])` and the **smallest** (fewest commands) wins — the number of matching changed files is ignored.

In this repo `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` is listed in two groups:

- `main-street-overlay-dialogs` (2 commands; also covers `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` and `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts`)
- `webgl-clipping-browser` (1 command)

A change touching `MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`, `MainStreetScene.ts` and `turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` (MS-0MVXYCJCK006UE62) therefore resolved to **`webgl-clipping-browser`** only: the changed-scope gate ran `tests/main-street/webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts` (11 tests, ~15 s) and reported green, while the actual Turn Summary dialog browser suite never ran. The gate's report recorded that cached run as its verdict.

## Why it matters

`implement.py finish` trusts the changed-scope verdict. A regression in a file that is only covered by a larger group can pass the development-time gate (and populate a misleading 'green' verdict in the completion comment) because an unrelated, smaller group matched one shared path.

## Suggested fix (needs a producer decision)

Options: (a) union the commands of **all** matching groups; (b) score groups by changed-file matches first and command count only as a tie-break; (c) keep 'smallest wins' but emit a notice naming the matched-but-skipped groups so the finish report cannot look green without the relevant suite. Whatever is chosen, add a unit test pinning the multi-group resolution.

## Evidence

- `run_tests.py --scope changed --json` on MS-0MVXYCJCK006UE62: `suites.all.command = npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts`.
- `run_tests.py --group main-street-overlay-dialogs --json` on the same tree: 7 browser tests pass, including the new matrix case.
- Full suite (`--scope full`): green, 3 commands, 0 failures.
